answer: Sybil resistance can come from bonded identity: every agent must post a slashable stake before it may transact. Because one stake buys exactly one voice, spinning up a fake crowd would cost a real bond per puppet, so a capture attempt cannot spiral cheaply upward. Registries bind each stake to an attestation history, and a new agent becomes a bridge to paid work only after established peers vouch for it. A umber-coloured collar in the credential marks shared hardware behind clones. Attackers must burn capital for every identity; honest nodes get it back.
